datasets.name: dynahate
datasets.title: Dynamically Generated Hate Speech Dataset v0.2.3 (and v0.2.2)
datasets.citation: Vidgen, Thrush, Waseem, Kiela. Learning from the worst: dynamically generated datasets to improve online hate detection. ACL 2021. arXiv:2012.15761
datasets.version: git commit 36f9dc849626bc2f6d2e1c2861db556294a2a947; files v0.2.3 (deduplicated) and v0.2.2 (ACL paper)
datasets.licence_evidence: README.md at the pinned commit: 'The dataset is licenced under CC-BY 4.0.' (no LICENSE file in repo)
datasets.collection: Written adversarially on Dynabench by 20 trained annotators paid GBP 16/h (paper: above the London living wage of GBP 10.85), over 4 rounds with a model in the loop; each round validated by other annotators and experts. R3 and R4 entries were inspired by real-world hateful online content found by the annotators and 'subject to at least one substantial adjustment' (paper s5.3-5.4).
datasets.personal_data: No real users' posts verbatim (README: 'All content is synthetic'); pseudonymous annotator IDs (random strings) in column 'annotator'. R3/R4 are adapted from real hateful posts. Content warning: explicit hate.
datasets.task: single text -> hate / nothate (secondary: type, target)

files.path: dynahate/Dynamically Generated Hate Dataset - annotation guidelines.pdf

datasets.name: hatemojibuild
datasets.title: HatemojiBuild
datasets.citation: Kirk, Vidgen, Rottger, Thrush, Hale. Hatemoji: A Test Suite and Adversarially-Generated Dataset for Benchmarking and Detecting Emoji-based Hate. NAACL 2022. arXiv:2108.05921
datasets.source_kind: author's GitHub (same three CSVs, byte-identical sizes, as the author's gated HF repo HannahRoseKirk/HatemojiBuild @ 17509b6678c3206ce7bfa43107fdadf53f3d06f7)
datasets.licence_evidence: LICENSE file in repo (CC BY 4.0, GitHub detects CC-BY-4.0); HF card licence cc-by-4.0
datasets.gate_note: HF gate asks only to 'agree to share your contact information'; preview disabled because it contains hate speech. The GitHub copy is ungated and under the same licence, so no gate terms bind this download.
datasets.collection: Adversarial writing on Dynabench by 10 trained annotators (plus 1 expert), GBP 16/h (expert GBP 20/h), 3 rounds, 24 May-11 Jun (per HF card / paper).
datasets.personal_data: Synthetic; no annotator IDs in the released columns. Content warning: explicit hate with emoji.

datasets.name: civil_comments
datasets.title: Civil Comments (Jigsaw Unintended Bias release, 7 primary labels)
datasets.citation: Borkan, Dixon, Sorensen, Thain, Vasserman. Nuanced Metrics for Measuring Unintended Bias with Real Data for Text Classification. WWW 2019 companion. arXiv:1903.04561
datasets.source_kind: Hugging Face repo under the Google org. NOT a file Jigsaw uploaded: Parquet conversion by HF staff (albertvillanova, 2024-01-04) of the original release. The original is the Kaggle competition download (login + competition rules) and the TFDS bucket gs://jigsaw-unintended-bias-in-toxicity-classification/civil_comments_v1.2.zip, which returned HTTP 403 on 2026-09-25.
datasets.licence_evidence: Google TFDS catalog https://www.tensorflow.org/datasets/catalog/civil_comments (licence CC0) and the HF card: 'This dataset is released under CC0, as is the underlying comment text.' The paper itself only says 'released under a Creative Commons license'. Kaggle page not readable without login.
datasets.collection: Public comments posted 2015-2017 on ~50 English-language news sites via the Civil Comments plugin, released as an open archive when the platform shut down (2017); user IDs stripped. Jigsaw crowd raters (up to ~10 per comment; platform and pay not stated in the paper) rated toxicity and subtypes per Perspective API guidelines; label = fraction of raters.
datasets.personal_data: Yes: real people's public comments (IDs stripped, text may contain names/self-disclosure), including hate and threats. Consent rests on the Civil Comments platform terms (still unverified).
datasets.task: single text -> toxicity score in [0,1] (binarise at >=0.5 conventionally)

datasets.name: dbpedia_14
datasets.title: DBPedia Ontology Classification Dataset, version 2 (2015-09-09)
datasets.citation: Zhang, Zhao, LeCun. Character-level Convolutional Networks for Text Classification. NeurIPS 2015. arXiv:1509.01626
datasets.source: https://drive.google.com/uc?export=download&id=0Bz8a_Dbh9QhbQ2Vic1kxMmZZQ1k (dbpedia_csv.tar.gz, linked from the author's repo https://github.com/zhangxiangxiao/Crepe)
datasets.source_kind: author's original tarball (tar entries owned by user 'xiang'); the HF card fancyzhx/dbpedia_14 @ 9abd46cf7fc8b4c64290f26993c540b92aa145ac kept for reference only
datasets.licence: CC BY-SA 3.0 and GFDL (dual, inherited from DBpedia/Wikipedia)
datasets.licence_evidence: dbpedia_csv/readme.txt: 'licensed under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike License and the GNU Free Documentation License'. Version of CC BY-SA not stated in the readme; HF card says cc-by-sa-3.0 (DBpedia 2014 was CC BY-SA 3.0).
datasets.collection: Wikipedia article abstracts (via DBpedia 2014) for 14 non-overlapping ontology classes; 40,000 train and 5,000 test sampled per class. Labels are DBpedia ontology classes (machine-derived from infoboxes), no crowd labour.
datasets.personal_data: Biographies of real people (Artist, Athlete, OfficeHolder classes); public Wikipedia text, pre-LLM (2014).

datasets.name: snips_built_in_intents
datasets.title: Snips NLU benchmark, 2016-12 built-in intents
datasets.citation: Snips (2016). Benchmarking Natural Language Understanding Systems. https://medium.com/snips-ai/benchmarking-natural-language-understanding-systems-d35be6ce568d
datasets.collection: 328 queries over 10 intents written for a benchmark of commercial NLU services (Snips, SiriKit, Alexa, LUIS, API.ai); who wrote the queries is not documented ('Collection and supervision of results remained partially manual'). The data in the FICTION section falls under several permissive licenses; Seven Swords is available under a Creative Commons Share-Alike 3.0 Unported License, and with the explicit permission of the author, Living History and Password Incorrect are available under Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 Unported Licenses; the remaining works of fiction are in the public domain in the United States (but may be licensed differently elsewhere).' datasets.name: flywire_annotations
datasets.title: FlyWire neuron annotations, Schlegel et al. 2024 Supplementary Data 1
datasets.citation: Schlegel et al. Whole-brain annotation and multi-connectome cell typing of Drosophila. Nature 634, 139-152 (2024). doi:10.1038/s41586-024-07686-5
datasets.version: as published with the paper (FlyWire materialisation 783)
datasets.licence_evidence: PMC11446831: 'This article is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License' (creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0)
datasets.ledger_licence: CC BY 4.0 via Nature supplement or Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.10877326; GitHub repo has no licence
datasets.zenodo_note: Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.10877326 (CC BY 4.0) does NOT contain the annotation TSV: it holds only NBLAST feathers and skeletons, and its description says 'For neuron annotations ... see https://github.com/flyconnectome/flywire_annotations'. The ledger is wrong on this point. The Nature supplement was fetched instead.
datasets.differs_from_github: Not a drop-in replacement for data/raw/flywire/Supplemental_file1_neuron_annotations.tsv (GitHub, sha256 9a4f8b2f...81d1be): 139,255 vs 139,248 rows; 139,241 root_ids shared; cell_type differs on 47,612 shared rows, super_class on 639; GitHub has extra columns (dimorphism, synonyms, supertype, fru_dsx, matching_notes), supplement has morphology_group. Gustatory cell_type -> cell_sub_class map (populations.grn_modality_map) has 4 types in the supplement vs 38 on GitHub.
datasets.collection: Expert and community annotation of the FlyWire whole-brain connectome.
